question: Which data repairs does this database carry, and why?
rule: a repair enters this file only after its cause is closed in code; every entry names the place that was fixed. Applying a repair by hand fixes it once; putting it in the rebuild graph makes it a rule, which matters because the intermediate CSV still carries the row the new code no longer produces.

repairs.why: A replicon row with no identifier. `gbk_files/NZ_QXDB01000002.1.gbk` is 0 bytes (a download that stopped half way in December 2024), so no record could be parsed and the row that was written carried nucleotide_id=''. Something with no identifier cannot be the UNIT of the replicon table, and this row made every per-replicon denominator one too large (17,074 instead of 17,073). No ro/neighbour/operon/taxon row depends on it, so deleting it loses no observation. The FACT that a requested record never arrived is not deleted: it is now declared in `genomic_context/unreadable_files.csv`.
repairs.fixed_in: extract_genomic_context.py: a file whose identifier cannot be parsed is now given `status='unreadable'` and NO replicon row is written
